title: Cohen–Gabber presentations with an etale open meeting the special fibre
statement: Let $A$ be a complete Noetherian normal local domain of dimension $d\geq2$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], with separably closed residue field [def-kun-separably-closed]. There are a normal domain $A'$, an injective ring map $A\to A'$ finite as a module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], a coefficient ring $\Lambda$, and $r\geq1$, with an injective module-finite local map $R=\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]\to A'$ inducing an isomorphism on residue fields [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. In equal characteristic one can take $A'=A$, $\Lambda$ a field, and $r=d$. In mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, $\Lambda$ is a complete discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic $p$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and $r=d-1$. In both cases $\Lambda$ has separably closed residue field, and there is $f\in R$ with nonzero image in $(\Lambda/\mathfrak m_\Lambda)[[t_1,\ldots,t_r]]$ such that $R[1/f]\to A'[1/f]$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. For $0\leq j\leq r$, the ring $\Lambda[[t_1,\ldots,t_j]]$ is complete Noetherian regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], of dimension $j$ in the field case and $j+1$ in the discrete valuation case.

source.place: Expose IV, Theorem 2.1.1 and Remarks 2.1.2 (equal characteristic p>0); Theorem 4.2.2 and proof 4.2.5 (mixed characteristic); equal characteristic zero: Stacks algebra.tex Tag 032D, lemma-complete-local-Noetherian-domain-finite-over-regular (field case R_0=k[[X_1,...,X_d]], finite, residue isomorphism), generic etaleness being automatic in characteristic zero; Expose V 3.1.3 for the regular power-series base. No prime-to-ell degree assertion is made.
